name: StationGodMCP
instructions: Device and IC tools reach every device in the world: omit gateway_id or pass 'world'. A StationGod Gateway id narrows a call to the devices on that gateway's data networks. Start with list_devices or describe_device before reading or writing logic. Inventory, clock and console tools need no gateway. Large replies: every tool that can answer a lot takes output_file, written by this server, and fields and omit, applied by the game as it writes the reply. output_file: true (or a file name, letters/digits/-/_/., no folders) writes the whole reply as indented JSON to a file and answers only a pointer {output_file (the full path), bytes, tool, counts (each top-level list's length), summary (the reply's short top-level values), in_file_only (top-level keys too large to repeat), truncated (as below)}; read the file with your own tools. The folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\StationGodMCP\output unless the server was started with --output-dir or STATIONGODMCP_OUTPUT_DIR; files older than 7 days, and beyond the newest 200, are deleted. A named file is overwritten. Errors are always answered inline. fields: [names] keeps only those keys in each entry of the reply's top-level lists (e.g. find_things fields ["reference_id", "position"]); a dotted name is a path read from each entry, through nested objects and lists at any depth (inspect_slots occupant.prefab_name, find_items held_in.reference_id), or from one list's entries when it starts with that list's name (things.position.x; dictionary keys keep their case, results.logic.Temperature); a name no entry has is listed in fields_unmatched. omit: [paths] leaves those keys out wherever they are, each a path from the reply's top (get_ic_status omit ["lua.log", "pins"]; a list on the way applies the rest to each entry: connections omit ["members.position"]); a path that matched nothing is listed in omit_unmatched. Default replies are kept small: a tool lists a short page or the first entries of a long list. Every reply ends with truncated: one entry per list it holds back, {list, returned, total, more (the exact argument that gets the rest, with its maximum)}, at_least true when total is a lower bound; truncated [] means nothing was held back. It survives fields, omit and output_file (the pointer carries it); read it before concluding you saw everything. list_limits {list: count} keeps more of a list the reply cut by default. Prefer filters, limit, fields and omit first; use output_file when you need all of a large reply. The player (the default from_id, to_id and credit card holder, a 'player' argument, near_player_m, local_player and player in replies, player_vitals) is the local player when the game has one; without one (a dedicated server) it is the one connected, living player in the world when there is exactly one, and with none or several those calls refuse no_local_player, saying which. The camera and screen (looking_at, crosshair, on_face_i_look_at, the player frame, looking, highlight, show_preview) are that player's: this game's own, or on a dedicated server the view the player's own StationGod shares and the screen it draws on (StationGod is optional there; without it those calls refuse no_view, saying why).
